speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for confirming your post-tympanoplasty symptoms. To better understand the nature of this shooting pain and the difficulty wearing earrings, can you describe if the pain is triggered by cold air or pressure changes, and does it radiate to your jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Neuralgia secondary to post-tympanoplasty nerve entrapment.

The shooting pain triggered by eating is classic for this condition, where the auriculotemporal nerve gets compressed by scar tissue near the tragus. The difficulty wearing earrings is likely due to residual tenderness or neuroma formation at the piercing site. Have you noticed any facial muscle weakness or changes in your jaw movement on the right side?
